parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime for a visitor shows no documented trans-specific criminal offence, no documented arrests or police targeting of trans people, and no facility or document-based exclusion. The visitor's home documents are used, and no source describes border marker flags. Visible official acceptance (head-of-state endorsement of Pride) and 2024 protection decrees that name trans people raise the rating. Against this, gender identity is absent from general anti-discrimination and hate-crime law, custody rules have no gender-identity safeguard, verbal abuse in some public medical services is reported, and family and community violence is documented. No state enforcement of the protection decrees in trans cases is sourced. The result is a Reduced Risk tier, below protective-statute jurisdictions.

entry_documents.exposure: No border marker-flagging or screening practice for trans travellers is documented. Home-issued documents are the operative instrument, and no domestic route exists to alter a marker.
entry_documents.protection: Home passport is accepted without a documented domestic marker challenge; no gender-recognition barrier is documented for visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: A visitor whose passport marker differs from presentation has no documented border treatment; the gap is an open question, not a known exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Penal execution rules protect only sexual orientation, with no gender-identity safeguard. Custody placement for trans detainees is undocumented, so a detained visitor faces an unanswered placement question.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No trans-specific arrest pattern or police targeting is documented. Police non-discrimination decrees cover sexual orientation only.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention rules are sexual-orientation-only, so a visitor detained for any reason meets a structural gap in gender-identity safeguards.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No law bars trans people from public facilities. Facility-access rules are not documented as restrictive; no universal-exposure measure is recorded.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Documented absence of facility bans; 2024 decrees bar disclosure of gender identity without authorisation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Confidentiality duties apply to social workers, not to all public services, so disclosure risk outside social services remains an open question.

care_services.exposure: Reported verbal abuse and discrimination in some public services, including medical centres, with no locality breakdown. No documented care denial to trans visitors.
care_services.protection: Health policy must be non-discriminatory on gender identity, including the 2022 health-law amendment.
care_services.interaction: Paper protection exists, but reported practice diverges. Remedies for trans patients are not documented as working.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No state threat-framing against trans people is documented. The 2017 foreign report notes no government action to prevent discrimination or violence.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Official endorsement of Pride; 2024 protection instruments explicitly name transgender people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Positive official signalling coexists with documented inaction on discrimination, so the protective signal is partly symbolic.

minors_guardians.exposure: Transgender students are reported more likely to be bullied and to leave school. A 2024 procedure notes transgender children may face greater risk of stigma and violence.
minors_guardians.protection: A 2024 ministerial decree requires protection services for children regardless of gender, and case managers must respond on the basis of gender identity.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor travelling with a guardian meets these child-protection duties, but the 2023 children's law and 2024 procedures are not documented as tested in trans cases.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Violence against trans people is documented as family and community-based, with harassment reported. The 86 per cent figure is from a 57-person self-selected sample and cannot be used as a rate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Physical abuse in public or by authorities is described as uncommon. Pride marches occur without documented violence against trans participants.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Family-sphere violence reaches visitors mainly through a home-country family, not through local institutions; street exposure to foreigners is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Gender identity is absent from general anti-discrimination and hate-crime law. The 2017 constitutional clause was removed. Partner recognition is closed, so a same-sex-read partner has no documented residence or next-of-kin standing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Domestic-violence law covers intimate partners regardless of gender, without a cohabitation requirement. No enforced trans-specific remedy is documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Partner exposure and absent gender-identity recourse compound for a visitor travelling with a partner who could be read as same-sex.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both show documented health-care friction and misgendering with no custody threat. The dossier here lacks a documented working complaint route for trans patients and has custody rules with no gender-identity safeguard, so it sits slightly lower or similar. Its visible official endorsement and 2024 decrees naming trans people lift it at least to the same tier.

The 0.55-E case has documented ejection from transit and selective scrutiny. The dossier here documents no equivalent public-space removal or service denial, and its state signalling is more positive. It therefore sits higher than 0.55-E.

The 0.75-D case has an equality statute covering gender identity and a police review board with enforcement. This dossier lacks a gender-identity anti-discrimination law and documents no enforcement in trans cases, so it sits below 0.75-D.

parsed.synthesis: Visitor-facing exposure is low: no criminal statute, no documented police targeting, no facility or document exclusion, and visible official acceptance. The main drags are structural. Custody rules have no gender-identity safeguard, gender identity is missing from hate-crime and general anti-discrimination law, and partner recognition is closed for same-sex-read couples. Reported verbal abuse in public medical services and family-sphere violence are documented, but the family-sphere exposure reaches visitors mainly through home ties. The 86 per cent figure is unusable as a rate. Protective 2024 decrees are positive but not shown to be enforced in trans cases. Overall, the record supports a Reduced Risk rating.
